Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
229 PM EST Thu Nov 12 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Mountain snow forecast continues to trend downward over the 
Alleghenies for tonight through Saturday. Most thunderstorm 
activity has now transitioned north of the region, with 
intermittent showers continuing into tonight. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) First snowfall for parts of the Alleghenies with spotty showers 
& brisk conditions elsewhere through Saturday. 


- 2) Cooler temperatures and dry conditions expected through mid
  week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... First snowfall for parts of the Alleghenies with 
spotty showers & brisk conditions elsewhere through Saturday.

Overall not too much of a change from the morning forecast package 
outside of decreasing PoPs and filtered breaks of sunshine east of 
the mountains. Still monitoring the progression of low pressure 
ejecting east out of the southwest PA this afternoon. The low is 
currently located in the vicinity of of Altoona/Latrobe, PA over the 
Laurel Highlands and will continue to trek east toward the southern 
NJ/Delmarva coast late tonight into Friday. At the surface, is a 
lead shortwave trough which produced a brief round of severe weather 
in Cecil Co. MD earlier this afternoon and the potential for 
tornadoes over Delaware Valley/NJ heading into the early evening 
period given increased convergence. Northeast MD is now out of the 
severe weather risk this afternoon although a few more showers 
cannot be ruled out along the MD/PA/DE border through this evening 
as the low and it's associated front work east. Most areas east of 
the mountains continue to see downsloping flow which in turn has 
shredded PoPS and led to filtered breaks in cloud cover. Mountain 
locations are also mostly dry with pockets of showers and drizzle 
mainly from Bayard, WV points south given the fetch behind the low 
pressure system off of Lake Erie and Lake Michigan. As the low 
pushes east and northwesterly flow increase expect the coverage of 
showers eventually changing to snow showers over the Alleghenies to 
increase heading into Friday and Friday night.

00, 06, and 12z guidance has backed off quite a bit in regards to 
snow amounts with the bulk of the accumulations stretched over a 24 
to 30 hour period. Marginal temperatures at onset will also impact 
accumulations with most of the snow falling Friday morning into 
Friday afternoon. Guidance has come into better agreement in lagging 
snow shower chances over the mountains through at least Saturday 
before things begin to shutdown as high pressure builds back into 
the region. Friday night into Saturday looks to be the most 
impactful snow at least when it comes to untreated surfaces given 
temperatures below freezing and snow ratios on the order of 12:1 
increasing to 14-16:1 at times. These will of course be maximized at 
elevations above 2000 feet and in particularly the upslope favored 
zones of western Garrett, western Pendleton, and western Grant 
counties. If travel disruptions were to materializes, expect impacts 
to US-219 from the MD/PA line to WV line, US-48 from Mount Storm, WV 
west to Davis, WV, and US-33 west of Franklin, WV. Snow 
accumulations will remain on the order of a coating to 2" with 
the greater probabilities of 1-2" with localized 3" amounts 
above 3000 feet pending any squalls/streamers (mainly late
Friday night through Saturday midday).

Temperatures will begin to drop tonight as this frontal passage 
moves through, continuing to get chillier into the weekend as winds 
gust up to 25 knots Friday-Sunday. Additional rain showers are 
likely primarily north & east of the I-70 corridor throughout the 
day Friday. Most rain east of the Blue Ridge likely diminishes by 
Friday evening, with temperatures becoming noticeably colder between 
Friday and Sunday. Overnight lows range in the upper 20s to mid 30s 
areawide through the weekend, with daytime temperatures generally in 
the 40s to low 50s & remaining near freezing across the
mountains.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler temperatures and dry condtions expected into 
the middle of next week.

Upper level troughing remains over the east coast through early next 
week with upper level ridging pivoting overhead by midweek. At the 
surface, high pressure builds in from the west yielding dry 
conditions. Conditions dry out areawide on Sunday as winds weaken in 
the afternoon and upslope snow becomes less likely. As high pressure 
builds overhead, light winds can be expected through next week along 
with dry conditions areawide. As far as temperatures, below normal 
temperatures continue early in the week with high temperatures 
ranging from the 30s in the Alleghenies to the mid 50s in the metros 
on Sunday. As high pressure settles overhead, temperatures moderate 
with highs in the 50s and 60s by Wednesday. Overnight low 
temperatures drop into the 20s to low 30s for most with only those 
in the metros staying in the mid 30s. The growing season ends this 
weekend so frost/freeze headlines will not be issued. 

&&

.AVIATION /19Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Predominantly VFR conditions are expected across the area through 
the 00z TAF period outside of terminals west of KCBE and KSHD. 
Overall aviation conditions will improve with scattered to broken 
ceilings this afternoon and evening ahead of the low pressure system 
ejecting out of southwest PA. An isolated to scattered shower 
remains possible at terminals north of a line from KOKV to KDCA. Any 
shower activity will be light between now-23z/2-6pm as the front 
pushes through. 

Upslope showers will continue over the mountains tonight before 
changing to snow showers Friday into Saturday. Expect a brief period 
low cigs and vsbys prior to daybreak for all terminals outside of 
CHO with improvements Friday afternoon and evening as drier air 
pushes into the region. Sub-VFR conditions will remain over the 
mountains through Saturday as upslope snow showers continue. 

Expect west to southwest winds this afternoon to shift to the 
north and northwest this evening. Gusts will increase to around 
20 kts overnight with 20-30 kt gusts out the northwest for 
Friday and Saturday as cold air advection funnels in. BKN- OVC 
stratocumulus deck is expected Fri-Sun during the day, with 
additional showers possible primarily at KBWI & KMTN during the 
day Friday as the cold front/low pressure push further offshore.

Northwest winds on Sunday blow around 10 knots with gusts between 15 
and 20 knots expected. Winds diminish overnight with light northwest 
winds expected on Monday. Surface high pressure building overhead 
yields VFR conditions both days. 

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisories go into effect for all waters at 6pm 
tonight and continue through Friday. Winds strengthen this 
evening in the wake of a strong cold front, with frequent gusts 
up to 20 knots expected. Winds strengthen further Friday into 
Saturday with gusts up to 30 kts possible. Winds may diminish 
some on Sunday, but gusts up to 20 knots remain possible. 

Small Craft Advisories are likely to continue into Sunday as gusty 
northwest winds continue. Winds diminish overnight into Monday and 
are expected to drop below SCA criteria. 

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
A Coastal Flood Advisory has been issued for Annapolis (Anne 
Arundel County) between 2100-0300 UTC this evening, as strong 
northwesterly flow likely brings water levels to minor flood 
stage. Several other coastal sites are likely to see Action 
stage this evening correlating with high tide as winds shift 
northwest behind a strong cold front. A prolonged period of 
blowout tides is possible starting Friday through early next 
week as winds stay elevated behind the front.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...Small Craft Advisory from 6 PM this evening to 6 PM EST Friday 
     for MDZ008.
     Coastal Flood Advisory until 10 PM EST this evening for MDZ014.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 6 PM this evening to 6 PM EST Friday 
     for ANZ530>543.

&&

$$
